answer: The admission bond is time locked for 9 epochs, longer than any single challenge window, so capital cannot be cycled between aliases within one epoch. Locks are entered in zenith, expire in tundra, and willow lists each expiry. An adversary running 138 aliases thus needs 40 simultaneously locked bonds rather than one rotating pool. A farm of 1821 identities would post 3932 proofs and burn roughly 13 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
